Title: The Actor Was the Expensive Part
Description: AI video models like ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 can now generate finished film, sound and image together, in a single pass from reference material, holding characters and voices consistent across shots. That collapses the real cost of moviemaking, which was never the camera but everything physical in front of it. This post works through what follows: budget stops gating imagination, historical accuracy becomes a setting, characters get recast after the fact, film sagas stop aging wrong, and a great deal of human craft becomes worth much less, all at the same time.

Title: Is the Industrial Revolution a good precedent for explosive economic growth today?
Description: One line of evidence that AI might lead to explosive economic growth is the precedent set by the Industrial Revolution. For hundreds of years — 1252 to 1652, to be precise — the compound annual growth rate of per capita real GDP in the UK was around 0.07%. It then began to accelerate, settling into a new compound rate of around 1.02% per year by 1850, which it held until 1913. In other words, growth accelerated by roughly 15 times before; the argument goes that this should make us humble about predicting it can’t happen again, and perhaps we should be open to accelerations of 10 times or more today.
